title: Chesterton - The Sign Of the Broken Sword

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown poses a riddle-based method of reasoning to work through the mystery.
evidence.quote: Where does a wise man hide a pebble?

evidence.paraphrase: The priest sets out a structured method separating public knowledge from his private findings.
evidence.quote:
I must divide it into two parts," remarked the priest. "First there is
      what everybody knows; and then there is what I know.

evidence.paraphrase: Brown describes collecting multiple pieces of evidence and presenting them in logical order.
evidence.quote:
There are three more bits of evidence," said the other, "that I have dug
      up in holes and corners; and I will give them in logical rather than
      chronological order.

evidence.paraphrase: Brown reframes the key question by asking who witnessed the sword intact, a deductive turning point.
evidence.quote:
No," cried Father Brown, with a sharp voice like a pistol shot; "but who
      saw his unbroken sword?

evidence.paraphrase: Brown reasons from the timing of the colonel's wound that the sword must have been broken before the fighting.
evidence.quote:
He was struck long before the troops came to
      close quarters. But he saw St. Clare\u2019s sword broken. Why was it broken?
      How was it broken? My friend, it was broken before the battle.

evidence.paraphrase: Flambeau reacts with revulsion after offering his own theory.
Flambeau shudders as he recalls Dante's lowest circle for traitors.
evidence.quote: The traitors," said Flambeau, and shuddered.

evidence.paraphrase: Flambeau expresses disgust upon seeing the inn named for St. Clare.
evidence.quote:
I thought we had done with the leper," cried Flambeau, and spat on the
      road.

evidence.paraphrase: The general sends hundreds of soldiers to die in order to cover up his crime.
evidence.quote:
In twenty minutes eight hundred English soldiers were marching down
      to their death.

evidence.paraphrase: Brown extends the hide-a-leaf logic to concealing a corpse among many corpses.
evidence.quote:
And if a man had to hide a dead body, he would make a field of dead
      bodies to hide it in.

evidence.paraphrase: The murderer reasons that creating many deaths will conceal his single murder.
evidence.quote:
He had killed, but not silenced. But his imperious
      intellect rose against the facer; there was one way yet. He could make the
      corpse less unaccountable. He could create a hill of corpses to cover this
      one.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrative contrasts the expected behavior of two famous men with their apparently inexplicable actions.
evidence.quote:
One of the wisest men in the world acted like an idiot
      for no reason. One of the best men in the world acted like a fiend for no
      reason.

evidence.paraphrase: Brown contrasts the public reverence for St. Clare with the contempt of those who knew the truth.
evidence.quote:
Millions who never knew him shall love
      him like a father\u2014this man whom the last few that knew him dealt
      with like dung.
